accent_note: Acute on the penult (πέμ-). It does not change to grave because the accent is not on the ultima.

Headword ἀγορά has an acute on the ultima in isolation; before a following word with no intervening punctuation it becomes grave (ἀγορὰ). Groton prints the genitive ending -ᾶς with circumflex; ἡ is unaccented.

Headword ἐπιστολή has an acute on the ultima in isolation; before a following word with no intervening punctuation it becomes grave (ἐπιστολὴ). Groton prints the genitive ending -ῆς with circumflex; ἡ is unaccented.
Headword ἡσυχίᾱ has an acute on the penult (-χί-), so it does not change to grave. Groton's abbreviated genitive ending -ᾱς is unaccented here; ἡ is unaccented.

Headword θεά has an acute on the ultima in isolation; before a following word with no intervening punctuation it becomes grave (θεὰ). Groton prints the genitive ending -ᾶς with circumflex; ἡ is unaccented.

Headword σκηνή has an acute on the ultima in isolation; before a following word with no intervening punctuation it becomes grave (σκηνὴ). Groton prints the genitive ending -ῆς with circumflex; ἡ is unaccented.
Headword χώρᾱ has an acute on the penult (χώ-), so it does not change to grave. Groton's abbreviated genitive ending -ᾱς is unaccented here; ἡ is unaccented.
